summary:
FLAMEINGO is an advanced Earth Observation web platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to resolve a critical 25-year scientific divide: harmonizing active fire hotspot observations between retiring MODIS (1km) sensors and modern VIIRS (375m) constellations. 

While satellites have tracked fire regimes since 2000, raw records cannot be compared directly due to optical pixel smear, varying sensitivities, and constellation expansions that create artificial 10x surges in modern fire counts. FLAMEINGO solves this with a mathematically grounded 2-tier harmonization engine. Tier 1 executes piecewise multi-sensor calibration across four satellite epochs (1.85x, 1.0x, 4.6x, 9.2x) directly over 96.2M real NASA FIRMS records. Tier 2 performs O(N) spatio-temporal event clustering (1.5km, 45 min) with physical peak Fire Radiative Power (FRP) envelopes.

FLAMEINGO delivers an interactive 25-Year Burning Activity Calendar, real-time climatological anomaly detection against multi-year medians, GPU-accelerated swipe comparison, interactive bounding-box drawing, and multi-format exports (GeoJSON, RFC 4180 CSV). It empowers emergency managers, scientists, and responders with dependable, sensor-independent wildfire intelligence.
details:
FLAMEINGO is an interactive platform that harmonizes 25 years of NASA active fire data into a single, standardized climate record. Raw FIRMS data shows an artificial surge in fire counts after 2012 due to the sensor transition from MODIS (1 km) to higher-resolution VIIRS (375 m) across Terra, Aqua, Suomi-NPP, and NOAA-20. FLAMEINGO corrects this discontinuity through multi-sensor piecewise normalization and spatio-temporal clustering (1.5 km, 45 minutes), aggregating fragmented satellite detections into coherent physical fire complexes.

The platform eliminates sensor bias so researchers, forest managers, and policymakers can assess true decadal wildfire trends rather than instrument artifacts. Instead of hiding the normalization logic, we built a transparent dual-mode interface where users can switch between harmonized fire complexes and raw satellite passes to inspect individual brightness temperatures, radiative power, and sensor weights. We specifically accounted for sparse fire regimes with zero-count protection and scaled Fire Radiative Power (FRP) alongside count normalization to keep energy metrics physically accurate.

The application is built with TypeScript, Next.js, and Tailwind CSS, using MapLibre GL for WebGL-accelerated map rendering. The backend runs on Node.js, querying over 96.2 million NASA FIRMS records stored in an AWS RDS PostgreSQL instance with PostGIS spatial indexing to deliver sub-second responses across multi-decadal queries.

Live Application: https://flameingo.ahmedmuneeb.com

Source Code: https://github.com/theahmedmuneeb/flameingo
